This is a hearty and flavoursome beef [[Cookbook:Stew|stew]] inspired by the Mediterranean. It is based on a dish cooked by [[w:Keith Floyd|Keith Floyd]] in his ''Floyd around the Med'' TV series. The olives make this a filling meal in itself, but it could be served with [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]] or simply with [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]] to mop-up the gravy.

==Ingredients==
* 500 [[Cookbook:g|g]] (1.1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) of lean [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]] stewing/braising steak (in steaks, not diced)
* 600 [[Cookbook:g|g]] (1.3 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) of green [[Cookbook:Olive|olives]], stones removed
* 6 large [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 1 large clove of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|Olive oil]]

==Procedure==
#In a large [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] or casserole dish, gently [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] the onion and garlic in plenty of good olive oil for a few minutes, taking care not to brown them.
#Season the beef well with [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] and black [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]] and immediately add to the pan. Fry until evenly sealed and lightly browned.
#Add the olives and tomatoes to the pan and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] gently for two hours with the lid on.
#Serve.

==Notes, tips and variations==
*If you buy olives in brine, it's a good idea to soak them in fresh water before use so that the resulting dish is not overly salty.
*Adding red [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]] or a dark [[Cookbook:Beer|beer]] such as a dunkel or stout could result in a richer gravy but may overpower the fresh flavour of the vegetables.
